items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And sometimes I’ll go back and listen to old Les Paul and go wow that’s like Charlie Christian.

ctx.x: Well you mentioned, amongst the things that you think about when you play, you think about sound. Is there a way that you can, as a bass player, how do you distinguish your own bass playing from any other thing.

That’s a very hard thing. I think it’s hard on any instrument these days, with all the influences out there. You know you’ve got to steal from the best. You know, you do, we all do. We’ve all had, listen I worked for Les Paul for quite a while. And sometimes I’ll go back and listen to old Les Paul and go wow that’s like Charlie Christian. You know what I mean? Like some of the really early stuff, with a little Django in there perhaps and other people that he was listening to at the time that were around. And…
Yeah, I think saxophone and trumpet players forget about that situation, that if you were going to fly to a gig and okay here’s your saxophone, it’s like, I can’t play that, or that’s tricky.
